subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@finly.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Alex / Sasha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- P95 latency on short, interactive prompts is sitting ~600ms end-to-end (user to response) and causes noticeable lag in the streaming chat UX.
- First-token streaming latency (time-to-first-chunk) often spikes and makes the UI feel sluggish.
- Peak traffic pattern: synchronous user interactions with bursts during market open — ~300 reqs/minute peak, ~150 concurrent active streaming sessions.
- Current infra: self-hosted Llama2-derived models on k8s (g4dn), limited batching and no prefix/KV cache. Autoscaling is reactive and slow.

Success criteria you called out:
- P95 generation latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<256 tokens).
- Streaming time-to-first-chunk <= 150ms.
- Sustained 150 concurrent streaming sessions at target latency without falling back to lower-quality model.
- Clear visibility into per-route token costs and latency breakdowns for procurement/fin ops.

What Redwood proposes for next steps (initial, short-term):
1) Technical baseline run: lightweight perf test (we simulate traffic profile you gave) to measure current p95 and streaming behavior.
2) SE deep-dive (Aditya) to review model configs, batching strategy, and KV/prefix cache feasibility.
3) 2-week PoC plan: small pilot on Redwood Dedicated (or hosted) to validate latency + concurrency targets.
4) Share SOC2 / security/infra docs in parallel for your procurement team.

Attachments: finly-quick-perf-snapshot.png (screenshot we referenced during demo).

Open questions (from our side):
- Can you share a representative short prompt set (anonymized) and a sample streaming session trace (if available)?
- Do you have strict cost targets per 1k tokens we'd need to hit for an acceptable solution?

Proposed calendar: can we block a 30–45m SE-runbook session Friday 9/24 or early next week? Aditya will lead that.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate next steps once you confirm timing.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and correct summary of our call. A few clarifications and answers to your open questions: 

- We can share an anonymized prompt set (about ~200 examples) and a single session trace. I’ll put those in a secure folder by EOD tomorrow.
- Cost target: we’re looking to keep inference compute spend for this workflow under $0.08 / 1k tokens (ballpark) as we evaluate vendor options. If Redwood has recommendations on batching/quantization tradeoffs that impact this number, please include in the PoC plan.
- For procurement: Sasha will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short security summary (encryption, data residency, KMS). Sasha — looping you in for next steps on that.

I’m available 9/24 10:00–12:00 PT for the SE session, or 9/25 in the morning. Either works — we prefer earlier rather than later.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming concurrency (SE notes)

Alex / team — jumping in with a short technical plan and what we’ll measure in the baseline run.

Baseline test (what we’ll run):
- Simulate 150 concurrent streaming sessions with the prompt mix you’ll provide. We’ll use a k6 script (attached: k6-streaming-script.sh) to reproduce time-to-first-chunk and steady-state throughput.
- Test model variants: full-fp16 baseline, 8-bit quant, and 4-bit quant (where compatible) to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Run three phases: cold-start (no cache), warm (prefill KV cache for repeated prefixes), and sustained burst (simulate market-open pattern).

What we’ll measure:
- P95 end-to-end generation latency for <256 token prompts.
- Time-to-first-stream-chunk (ms).
- CPU/GPU utilization and per-token cost estimates for each variant.
- Error rate / dropped-stream incidents under load.

Quick expectations from prior pilots: on modern A100-class infra + optimized kernels, we regularly see p95 ~120–220ms for short prompts with streaming-first-chunk <100–150ms at 150 concurrent sessions (depends on model size and batching). On g4dn-class instances without KV cache, p95 often sits >400–600ms — consistent with what you reported.

Immediate deliverables for the PoC (2-week):
1) Baseline report with metrics and clear pass/fail vs your success criteria.
2) Small config changes (batching, kernel tuning, quant profile) that we can apply to show single-digit to 2x improvements.
3) If baseline looks good, we’ll propose a scoped Dedicated footprint for sustained capacity and run a short pilot.

Attachments: k6-streaming-script.sh (load script stub).

Happy to run the Friday session (9/24 10:30 PT) — Marissa if that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short checklist of artifacts we need from Finly.
